title: Noetherian approximation for finite eta-modifications
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral affine scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. Let $p:Z\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with reduced geometric fibres [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Let $f:Z'\to Z$ be a finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] $\eta$-modification. Then there exist a normal integral Noetherian affine scheme $S_0$, a dominant morphism $S\to S_0$ carrying generic point to generic point, a flat finitely presented morphism $p_0:Z_0\to S_0$ with reduced geometric fibres, and a finite $\eta_0$-modification $f_0:Z'_0\to Z_0$, together with compatible isomorphisms identifying $(Z,Z',f)$ with the base change of $(Z_0,Z'_0,f_0)$ along $S\to S_0$ [def-pc-base-change]. Here Noetherian means quasi-compact and locally the spectrum of a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; $\eta$ and $\eta_0$ are the generic points of the respective integral bases. A $\xi$-modification is a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] which is an isomorphism on the fibre over $\xi$ and over an open $V$ of its target such that $V$ and its inverse image are schematically dense in target and source, respectively. For an open immersion $j:V\hookrightarrow T$, schematically dense means that $\mathcal O_T\to j_*\mathcal O_V$ is injective.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2 proof, printed p. 20, noetherian-reduction paragraph; §3.1 and Remark 3.1.1(i), printed pp. 14–15, for flatness and geometric reducedness; the remark following 3.1.1 permits the affine-base reduction. The model is required to retain finiteness and the generic-fibre isomorphism.

proof.text: Choose the affine Noetherian approximation $N$ of $S$ from [lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine]. Apply [lem-sbc-normal-finite-stage-diagram] to this $N$ and the normal integral $S$, obtaining integral normal stages $S_i$ finite over the affine stages of $N$, dominant projections $S\to S_i$, and the finite natural transformation to $N$. Each $S_i$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](b), and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]: a finite algebra is of finite type, as its module generators also generate it as an algebra. The cone is limiting by [lem-sbc-dominant-finite-refinement-limit]. The transition maps are affine since both source and target are affine. Reindex by a nonempty directed set using [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-limit-directed-reindex]. Dominance between integral schemes carries generic point to generic point. Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$; these dominant projections give injections $R_i\hookrightarrow R$ and $R=\varinjlim R_i$. The last equality follows from the universal property of the affine limit, by testing maps from affine schemes.

source.place: §3.1 normal Noetherian approximation; explicit normal refinement via finite normalization.

proof.text: Apply [thm-pd-spreading-out](1) to $p$ and this system to obtain $Z_a\to S_a$ of finite presentation with pullback $Z$. The stages are affine Noetherian, hence qcqs, and $Z_a$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-flat-finite-presentation] to obtain flatness at a later stage. Apply [lem-trf-geometrically-reduced-fibres-limit-descent] to obtain reduced geometric fibres at a later stage. Choose a common upper bound; finite presentation and flatness survive its base change by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3) and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. Call this model $p_0:Z_0\to S_0$. It has every required property of the family and base. It remains to construct the modification model. We shall show directly that $f$ is an isomorphism, without invoking the downstream eta-normality node, and then use the identity of $Z_0$.

Fix an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $Z$. If it is empty its inverse image is empty, so there is nothing to check; assume it nonempty. Its inverse image is affine, say $\operatorname{Spec}B$, and $B$ is finite over $A$ by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The algebra $A$ is finitely presented over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation]. Flatness gives $A\hookrightarrow A_K$, $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$, by [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free] with the trivial line bundle. Let $V$ be the common schematically dense isomorphism open of $f$. If a section of $B$ vanishes on the generic fibre, its restriction to $V\cap U$ vanishes, since the same torsion-freeness lemma applies to every affine open of that flat open. Schematic density of $f^{-1}V$ then makes that section zero. Thus $B\hookrightarrow B_K=A_K$, compatibly with $A\to B$, and we regard $A\subseteq B\subseteq A_K$. The generic fibre is reduced by hypothesis and field-extension injectivity (a vector-space basis); hence $A$ is reduced. No finite-presentation assertion about $B$ is used.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2: finite modification algebra and schematic density, made explicit before approximation.

proof.text: Choose finitely many $A$-algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ of $B$ (module generators suffice). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] choose monic polynomials $P_j(T)\in A[T]$ with $P_j(b_j)=0$. Since $B\subset A_K$, write all $b_j=a_j/r$ with a single $0\ne r\in R$ and $a_j\in A$, by multiplying their finitely many denominators. Choose a finite presentation $A=R[x_1,\ldots,x_m]/(g_1,\ldots,g_t)$. All coefficients of the $g_k$, of representatives of $a_j$, and of the coefficients of $P_j$ occur at one stage $R_i$. Put $A_i=R_i[x_1,\ldots,x_m]/(g_{1,i},\ldots,g_{t,i})$. Its base change is $A$. After increasing $i$, $\operatorname{Spec}A_i\to S_i$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-descend-flat-finite-presentation] and has reduced geometric fibres by [lem-trf-geometrically-reduced-fibres-limit-descent]. Flatness and geometric reducedness of $U\to S$ follow by restriction from $p$, so both descent hypotheses hold. Keep the same notation for the later coefficients and stage.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2 noetherian reduction; agent finite-generator construction replacing unjustified exact descent of an arbitrary finite algebra.

proof.text: Arrange also $P_{j,i}(a_{j,i}/r_i)=0$ in $(A_i)_{r_i}$. Here is the finite-data check: if $d_j=\deg P_j$, the polynomial $r^{d_j}P_j(a_j/r)$ is zero in $A$. In the displayed polynomial presentation it is a finite combination $\sum_k h_{jk}g_k$. Adjoin the finitely many coefficients of all $h_{jk}$ to the chosen stage. The equality of these polynomials then holds at a later stage (each coefficient equality in the filtered colimit holds eventually). After localization it gives the desired relation. Set $C_i=A_i[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(P_{j,i}(T_j),r_iT_j-a_{j,i})$. The monic relations bound each exponent of $T_j$ by $d_j-1$, so finitely many monomials generate $C_i$ as an $A_i$-module. The linear relations give $(C_i)_{r_i}\cong(A_i)_{r_i}$ by substitution $T_j\mapsto a_{j,i}/r_i$; the checked polynomial identities make the substitution well-defined. Sending $T_j$ to $b_j$ gives a surjection $C_i\otimes_{R_i}R\twoheadrightarrow B$.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2 noetherian reduction; explicit finite algebra with prescribed localization.

proof.text: Let $J_i=\{c\in C_i:r_i^Nc=0\text{ for some }N\}$ and $D_i=C_i/J_i$. This is an ideal: for two elements use the larger exponent, and multiplication preserves annihilation. Localization identifies $D_i$ with the image of $C_i$ in $(A_i)_{r_i}$. Flatness of $A_i$ over the domain $R_i$ gives $A_i\hookrightarrow(A_i)_{r_i}$ by [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free]. Consequently $A_i\subseteq D_i\subseteq(A_i)_{r_i}$ and $(D_i)_{r_i}=(A_i)_{r_i}$. The algebra $D_i$ is finite over $A_i$, being a quotient of $C_i$. Every element of $J_i$ maps to zero in $B$: its image is killed by a power of the nonzero $r\in R$, while $B\subset A_K$. Thus the preceding surjection factors as $D_i\otimes_{R_i}R\twoheadrightarrow B$. The construction requires a surjection, not an unjustified isomorphism after a possibly nonflat base change.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2 noetherian reduction; base-torsion quotient retaining the dense generic isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $Y_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ and $E_i=\operatorname{Spec}D_i$. These are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Let $W\subset Y_i$ be the isomorphism locus of the finite algebra inclusion $A_i\subset D_i$. It is open: its complement is the support of the finite module $D_i/A_i$, and if this module vanishes at a prime, one element outside that prime kills all of a finite list of generators, so it vanishes on a principal neighbourhood. It contains $D(r_i)$ and the generic fibre over $S_i$, since $(D_i)_{r_i}=(A_i)_{r_i}$. Moreover $\widetilde{D_i}\subset j_*\mathcal O_W$ for $j:W\hookrightarrow Y_i$: a section vanishing on $W$ vanishes after inverting $r_i$, and $D_i\hookrightarrow(A_i)_{r_i}$ remains injective upon localization on $Y_i$.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2: open isomorphism locus of the finite algebra, with the source base torsion removed.

proof.text: We show that $W$ contains the generic points of every fibre of $Y_i\to S_i$. At such a point [lem-trf-generic-fibre-points-smooth] supplies a smooth neighbourhood $T$. All local rings of $T$ are integrally closed domains by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-normal-ring-normal], since $S_i$ is normal. The open $D(r_i)$ is dense on $T$: flatness makes multiplication by $r_i$ injective on every affine chart, so localization is injective; an open on which $r_i$ were everywhere nilpotent would contradict that injection. For an affine open $H\subset T$, each section of the finite algebra $\widetilde{D_i}(H)$ is integral over $\mathcal O_T(H)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. Its restriction to $H\cap D(r_i)$ extends to $\mathcal O_T(H)$ by [lem-sbc-normal-dense-open-integral-section]. The injection into the $r_i$-localization makes the extension equal to the original section. Therefore $\widetilde{D_i}|_T=\mathcal O_T$, so $T\subset W$. All smoothness and extension inputs are applied to Noetherian schemes at this stage.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2: normal neighbourhoods at fibre-component generic points.

proof.text: If $y\notin W$ and $s$ is its image in $S_i$, then $s\ne\eta_i$, because $W$ contains the generic fibre. The local domain $R_{i,s}$ therefore has a nonzero maximal-ideal element, which is a nonzerodivisor, so its depth is at least one. The fibre local ring $F=\mathcal O_{(Y_i)_s,y}$ is reduced: its extension to an algebraic closure is reduced by the retained geometric-fibre hypothesis, and scalar extension of a field is injective. The point $y$ is not a generic point of a fibre component by the preceding step. Thus the local ring $F$ has dimension at least one. [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-reduced] gives depth $F\ge1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-depth-formula] to the flat local map $\mathcal O_{S_i,s}\to\mathcal O_{Y_i,y}$; both rings are Noetherian, and its closed-fibre ring is $F$. It gives depth $\mathcal O_{Y_i,y}\ge2$.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2: depth addition outside the isomorphism open.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-depth-two-hartogs-restriction] to $L=Y_i$, its open $W$, and $N=\mathcal O_{Y_i}$. It is quasi-coherent and finite on every affine chart and at every stalk; $Y_i$ is Noetherian, and the previous step verifies the depth hypothesis at every point of the complement. Hence $\mathcal O_{Y_i}=j_*\mathcal O_W$. Since $\mathcal O_{Y_i}\subseteq\widetilde{D_i}\subseteq j_*\mathcal O_W$, we get $D_i=A_i$. The surjection in step 6 now reads $A\twoheadrightarrow B$, and it is the original injective structure map $A\hookrightarrow B\subset A_K$. It is therefore an isomorphism. This holds for every affine open $U\subset Z$, so the inverses of the restrictions of $f$ glue (uniquely on overlaps) to an inverse of $f$. This argument establishes the needed conclusion directly and never cites the downstream eta-normality node, which depends on this item.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2: depth/Z-closure conclusion, applied to the approximating finite algebra.

proof.text: Take $Z^{\prime}_0=Z_0$ and $f_0=\mathrm{id}_{Z_0}$ for the family chosen in step 2. The identity is finite and proper directly from [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and [def-weil-proper-morphism], and is an $\eta_0$-modification with $V=Z_0$: restriction to the whole scheme is injective, including for the empty scheme. The model isomorphism $Z\cong Z_0\times_{S_0}S$, composed with the now proved isomorphism $f:Z^{\prime}\to Z$, supplies the second model isomorphism, and makes the diagram with $f_0$ commute. The dominant projection $S\to S_0$ takes the generic point to the generic point, as recorded in step 1. These are precisely the compatible base-change isomorphisms and all the required clauses.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.2 noetherian-reduction assertion; agent assembly of the exact model after the finite-algebra argument.
